hints: Radius $CP$ is perpendicular to tangent $PT$, creating right-angled triangle $\triangle CPT$ at $P$.
walkthrough:
The radius and tangent make perpendicular sides of a right triangle.
In right-angled triangle $\triangle CPT$ with right angle at $P$, the hypotenuse is $CT = 10$ and $CP = 5$:
$$CT^2 = CP^2 + PT^2$$
$$10^2 = 5^2 + PT^2 \implies PT^2 = 100 - 25 = 75$$
